regions.original: 一風堂監修 博多とんこつラーメン
regions.breakdown: 一風堂 (いっぷうどう, Ippūdō): Name of a famous ramen chain. 監修 (かんしゅう, kanshū): Supervision, supervised by. 博多 (はかた, Hakata): A district in Fukuoka known for its tonkotsu ramen. とんこつ (Tonkotsu): Pork bone broth, a type of ramen. ラーメン (rāmen): Ramen.

regions.original: 加熱後、ゆっくりスープへ 汁はね、こぼれに注意！
regions.translation: After heating, slowly pour into the soup. Beware of splashing and spilling soup!
regions.romanization: Kanetsu-go, yukkuri sūpu e. Shiru-hane, kobore ni chūi!
regions.breakdown: 加熱後 (かねつご, kanetsu-go): After heating. ゆっくり (yukkuri): Slowly. スープへ (sūpu e): To the soup. 汁はね (しるはね, shiru-hane): Soup splashing. こぼれ (kobore): Spill. に注意 (にちゅうい, ni chūi): Be careful of/about.

regions.original: セール実施中 30円引 セブン-イレブン 標準価格(税抜)からの値引き
regions.translation: Sale in progress. 30 yen discount. Discount from Seven-Eleven standard price (excluding tax).
regions.romanization: Sēru jisshi-chū. Sanjū-en biki. Sebun-Irebun hyōjun-kakaku (zeinuki) kara no nebiki.
regions.breakdown: セール (sēru): Sale. 実施中 (じっしちゅう, jisshi-chū): In progress. 30円引 (さんじゅうえんびき, sanjū-en biki): 30 yen discount. セブン-イレブン (Sebun-Irebun): Seven-Eleven. 標準価格 (ひょうじゅんかかく, hyōjun-kakaku): Standard price. (税抜) (ぜいぬき, zeinuki): (Excluding tax). からの (kara no): From. 値引き (ねびき, nebiki): Discount.
麺 (めん, men): Noodles. かため (katame): Hard, firm (often used for doneness of food).

regions.original: 加熱後は大変熱くなりますのでやけどにご注意ください。
regions.translation: It becomes very hot after heating, so please be careful not to get burned.
regions.romanization: Kanetsu-go wa taihen atsuku narimasu node yakedo ni go-chūi kudasai.
regions.breakdown: 加熱後 (かねつご, kanetsu-go): After heating. 大変 (たいへん, taihen): Very. 熱くなります (あつくなります, atsuku narimasu): Will become hot. ので (node): Because, so. やけど (yakedo): Burn (noun). にご注意ください (にごちゅういください, ni go-chūi kudasai): Please be careful of/about.

where_youd_see_it: On a packaged ramen bowl sold at a convenience store or supermarket.
cultural_note: Ippudo is one of Japan's most famous ramen chains, known for its Hakata-style tonkotsu ramen. Convenience stores often collaborate with popular restaurants to offer their signature dishes as ready-to-eat meals. '麺かため' (firm noodles) is a popular preference, especially for Hakata ramen, which traditionally uses thin noodles that cook quickly.
